articles.title: Japan’s Katayama warns of one-sided yen moves near 160, will coordinate with US Treasury
articles.desc: Katayama’s comments make intervention a more serious risk for anyone pushing dollar-yen above 160, especially as the US has now been confirmed as a willing partner. Expect choppy, headline-driven trading around that level, with dealers alert to any reports of rate checks. The underlying pressure on
articles.content: Katayama’s comments make intervention a more serious risk for anyone pushing dollar-yen above 160, especially as the US has now been confirmed as a willing partner. Expect choppy, headline-driven trading around that level, with dealers alert to any reports of rate checks. The underlying pressure on the yen remains, though, as rising Fed hike expectations keep rate differentials in the dollar’s favour. Oil matters too: higher crude prices raise Japan’s import bill and add to selling pressure on the yen, which is partly why Tokyo is bringing forward energy subsidies. --- Earlier: US Treasury bought yen in July, its first intervention since 1998, as yen nears 160 again --- With the yen back near 160, Katayama is reminding markets that Tokyo and Washington are working together on currencies, and that both have intervened before. Summary: Finance Minister Katayama says she is seeing one-sided, rapid moves in currency markets She will communicate with the US Treasury and respond appropriately She says the US and Japan shared a common stance on foreign exchange at their summit She declined to comment on intervention records The government is bringing forward winter utility subsidies, funded from reserve funds The yen is back near 160 per dollar, the level that triggered joint US-Japan intervention in the summer Main article: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama stepped up her warnings over the yen’s slide, saying she is seeing one-sided and rapid moves in currency markets and will stay in contact with the US Treasury to respond appropriately. Her comments come as the yen trades back near 160 per dollar, the level that drew joint US-Japan intervention in the summer. Katayama said the US and Japan set out a shared stance on foreign exchange at their summit, signalling that Tokyo sees Washington as aligned on the need to curb disorderly moves. She declined to comment on intervention records. That came shortly after the New York Fed disclosed that the US Treasury bought yen in July, its first yen-buying intervention since 1998, acting alongside Japan’s Ministry of Finance. The wording matters. Japanese officials typically use terms like “one-sided” and “rapid” when their concern is growing. Naming coordination with the US Treasury adds weight, because Washington has now shown it is willing to put its own money behind the yen. Japan’s vice finance minister for international affairs, Atsushi Mimura, gave a similar message on Thursday, warning that it was too early to forget the summer’s intervention. The yen’s renewed weakness reflects a familiar gap. A resilient US economy, stubborn inflation and rising expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December are supporting the dollar. The Bank of Japan, which raised rates in June and September, is widely expected to hike again in December. Until that gap narrows, officials are relying on words, and the threat of action, to slow the yen’s fall. Katayama also said the government has decided to bring forward subsidies for household utility bills this winter, paid for from reserve funds. The move aims to protect households from high energy costs. Elevated oil prices have pushed those costs up, and the weak yen makes them worse, because Japan imports almost all of its energy. For markets, the comments make it riskier for traders to push dollar-yen through 160. With both Tokyo and Washington signalling they are ready to act, the risk of another round of intervention is likely to keep the pair volatile around that level in the weeks before the BOJ’s December meeting. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Preserve All Evidence: With Huang Out At Nvidia, Democrats Want Every Record Of His Calls With Trump
articles.desc: Preserve All Evidence: With Huang Out At Nvidia, Democrats Want Every Record Of His Calls With Trump Hours before Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, two senior Senate Democrats told the Trump administration to preserve every record of its dealings with him, from his calls with Presid
articles.content: Preserve All Evidence: With Huang Out At Nvidia, Democrats Want Every Record Of His Calls With Trump Hours before Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, two senior Senate Democrats told the Trump administration to preserve every record of its dealings with him, from his calls with President Trump to a Commerce Department probe of the chip buyer whose executive, a suspected Chinese spy, he has acknowledged a relationship with. Sens. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), the Banking Committee's ranking member, and Chris Coons (D-DE) sent the Nov. 11 letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller. It asks all three offices to keep every record on exports of Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China "or to entities that may divert such chips to China," to confirm in writing by Nov. 17 that preservation directives have gone out, and to brief members of Congress on the risks the suspected operation posed. The list opens with the intelligence: every memorandum, assessment and briefing on the suspected operation involving Alice Huang, Jensen Huang or Megaspeed, including "the memorandum reportedly circulated to senior administration officials ahead of President Trump's visit to China in May 2026." The senators also want the "briefing materials, notes, and call transcripts" between Huang and Trump, and the records of Huang's meetings with senior officials on export controls, AI regulation and "proposed revenue-sharing or fee arrangements on chip sales." Megaspeed, a Singapore-based computing company, has bought more than $4.8 billion of Nvidia's advanced AI chips since June 2024, according to the letter, and is reportedly under Justice Department investigation for diverting them to China. Commerce's own case against it was halted after Nvidia's general counsel reached out to the agents running it, as we reported. The letter asks for the August 2025 correspondence between that general counsel, Tim Teter, and Jeffrey Kessler, Commerce's under secretary for industry and security, Teter's reported call to Kessler about Singapore's detention of a Megaspeed executive, and every record on the probe's transfer, suspension or termination. "This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government's ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security," Warren and Coons wrote. Officials at the White House, State and Commerce, they said, "were aware of concerns about NVIDIA, its relationship with Megaspeed, and the suspected Chinese intelligence operation, yet did not move to block the continued flow of advanced AI chips to Megaspeed." The senators also asked whether "prudent defensive counter-intelligence action was taken or national security recommendations were overruled," and demanded the records on whether to give Nvidia's leadership a counterintelligence warning at all. In a subsequent statement, Warren said that Huang's resignation "does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws." (we must have missed her letter about Dianne Feinsten's Chinese spy driver years ago) Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and NVIDIA’s board of directors still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls. It’s clear that the American people cannot rely on Big Tech billionaire CEOs to put our national security above their bottom line – which is why Congress must pass the AI Overwatch Act and other bipartisan bills to keep advanced American AI technology out of China’s hands. Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military. -Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) The request reaches back through every Trump-Xi meeting: the export-control talks ahead of the October 2025, May 2026 and September 2026 summits and the APEC meeting expected this month, Huang's seat on Trump's May 2025 Middle East trip, and Lutnick's invitation for Huang to meet Trump at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025. It also covers Nvidia's license applications under the Commerce Department's January 2026 rule on advanced computing chips, and the repeated suspensions of the rule extending export controls to affiliates of blacklisted companies. Rubio briefed Trump on the intelligence about Huang aboard Air Force One in May, the New York Times reported, on the trip to China that Huang joined; the White House disputed the account. Trump said Monday that Huang told him, "I had no idea that she was a spy," adding, "And I really believe him." House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast (R-FL) said Tuesday he was prepared to subpoena Huang if he didn't answer by Wednesday the request from Mast and Reps. John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Rick Crawford (R-AR) for a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18, as we noted. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said on the Senate floor Tuesday that "Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security," calling it "a dereliction of duty." Warren and Sen. Jim Banks (R-IN) on Sunday urged Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act in the defense bill and told Commerce to close export-control loopholes. Megaspeed, whose executive is at the center of the spy claims that Beijing has denied, said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with US export control laws "extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government." Huang resigned as president, CEO and director effective immediately on Thursday, a day after the Times reported a second affair, with an Nvidia vice president who reports to him. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Nvidia shares were down 11.9% in premarket trading, CNBC reported. The letter goes to the administration, not the company: its written confirmations are due Nov. 17, the day before the briefing House Republicans asked Huang to give. articles.title: UzAuto Motors' net profit falls 46.9% in nine months
articles.desc: UzAuto Motors' net profit fell 46.9% year on year to 1.867 trillion soums in January–September 2026, according to its financial statements.
articles.content: UzAuto Motors' net profit falls 46.9% in nine months — UzDaily.uz UzAuto Motors' net profit falls 46.9% in nine months UzAuto Motors' net profit fell 46.9% year on year to 1.867 trillion soums in January–September 2026, according to the company's financial statements published on the corporate information portal on 31 October. The automaker reported net profit of 3.517 trillion soums in the first nine months of 2025. The year-on-year decline was 1.65 trillion soums. Revenue from sales of cars, spare parts and other products fell 13.2% to 30.12 trillion soums from 34.71 trillion soums a year earlier. The cost of goods sold decreased by 11.2%, from 30.61 trillion to 27.17 trillion soums. As production costs declined more slowly than revenue, gross profit dropped 28.2% to 2.94 trillion soums from 4.1 trillion soums. Gross profit accounted for about 9.8% of revenue, compared with 11.8% a year earlier. Operating profit fell 56.2% to 1.3 trillion soums from 2.96 trillion soums. Meanwhile, selling expenses rose 14.3% to 1.17 trillion soums, compared with 1.02 trillion soums in January–September 2025. Profit before tax decreased 47.4% to 2.15 trillion soums from 4.09 trillion soums. Gains from positive exchange-rate differences fell 76% to 173.9 billion soums from 726.3 billion soums. At the same time, financial income increased to 1.2 trillion soums from 879.3 billion soums. Expenses for servicing loans and finance leases rose to 525.1 billion soums from 481.2 billion soums. UzAuto Motors' inventories were valued at 17.57 trillion soums as of 30 September 2026, compared with 11.7 trillion soums at the beginning of the year. Their value increased by 5.87 trillion soums, or 50.2%, over the nine-month period. Short-term trade and other accounts payable rose 95.5% to 5.99 trillion soums from 3.07 trillion soums at the beginning of the year. Meanwhile, cash and cash equivalents fell 80.6% to 257.2 billion soums from 1.33 trillion soums. The company's total assets increased to 35.31 trillion soums from 31.75 trillion soums over the period. Liabilities rose to 17.99 trillion soums from 16.2 trillion soums, while equity increased to 17.32 trillion soums from 15.55 trillion soums. articles.content: Jensen Huang Had to Go. The Real Question Is: Cui Bono? – PJ Media Jensen Huang Had to Go. The Real Question Is: Cui Bono? Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned today as CEO and, in an unusual step, also gave up his position on the company's board in the midst of a growing spy and sex scandal. So before we explore this story any further, let's acknowledge that Huang had to go. When you're the chief executive of the world's most important AI hardware company, and you've been (allegedly!) diddling the company's vice president of healthcare a purported Chinese intelligence asset, corporate harakiri is your only out. But that doesn't mean that, now that Jensen is out, we shouldn't ask: Because while Jensen's affairs were unbecoming and even dangerous, this is when things get truly interesting. For that, let's first go to French AI CEO (yes, they have a few of those, but not at scale) Brivael Le Pogam, who last month made headlines for warning Americans against voting Democrat because " "I'm not saying the [Huang] scandal is made up," he posted to on Thursday. "I'm saying: look at who is using it, and for what." Le Pogam continued: "To understand, you have to ask one question. What does the power of what I call the globalists actually rest on? Not money. Not weapons. A monopoly: the monopoly on expertise." The technocracy in Brussels and Washington, the big international institutions, the NGOs, the major newsrooms, the consulting firms: the whole system lives off an asymmetry. They know, you don't. They read the 400-page reports, you don't. They interpret the numbers, you live with the consequences. They write the rules, and you pay lawyers to understand them. Hayek saw it: central power feeds on the pretense of a knowledge no one really has. For decades, that pretense was impossible to challenge. It took years of study, networks, resources. Any citizen can audit a budget in ten minutes. Read an EU directive and see every consequence. Check an official statistic. Tear apart a junk study. Draft a legal challenge. Build a company alone, without asking anyone for permission. The asymmetry disappears. And with it, the monopoly. My Balkanization Plans Are Much Clearer After Last Week The GOP’s War Plan for Shattering the Democratic Party Coalition in 5 Easy Steps The blogosphere broke the news gatekeeper monopoly a quarter of a century ago and democratized the discovery and (most importantly) the distribution of information. Superintelligence promises to do the same for expertise — and none too soon, because our so-called experts aren't so expert these days. They've mostly built regulatory moats around their power and income streams. The coming revolution — provided we don't snuff it out in a fit of self-destructive populism and Chinese influence — promises to destroy all kinds of monopolies on expertise. This is from an Instapundit item I posted earlier today: Microsoft's diagnostic AI solved 83% of 304 complex New England Journal of Medicine cases. Generalist physicians with reference materials solved 36%. We need to get this technology into clinics safely and fast. We need to stop making people wait for the right answers. — Peter H. Diamandis, MD (@PeterDiamandis) Patients could be informed and empowered like never before, and a single doctor armed with AI could care for a seemingly impossible number of patients. And provide them with much more effective care, too. "If you don't get your s**t together," Ken Berry, M.D. , "there will be one hourly-wage doctor supervising an LLM that's treating a thousand patients, and a lot of doctors looking for work." And that's just one profession — a guild, really — currently surrounded by impenetrably high walls. articles.title: Azerbaijan, World Bank explore cooperation priorities
articles.desc: Baku, November 12, AZERTACOn November 12, Azerbaijani Finance Minister Sahil Babayev met with a World Bank delegation comprising Rolande Pryce, the Bank’s Regional Director for the South Caucasus, and Abebe Adugna, its Regional Director for Prosperity in Europe and Central Asia. The talks covered ma
articles.content: Baku, November 12, AZERTACOn November 12, Azerbaijani Finance Minister Sahil Babayev met with a World Bank delegation comprising Rolande Pryce, the Bank’s Regional Director for the South Caucasus, and Abebe Adugna, its Regional Director for Prosperity in Europe and Central Asia. The talks covered macroeconomic stability, fiscal sustainability, economic diversification, public financial management, reforms in state-owned enterprises and other issues of mutual interest. Babayev reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s commitment to its long-term partnership with the World Bank, highlighting the Bank’s contribution to the country’s economic development, institutional reforms and public sector modernization. He noted that the 2025–2029 Country Partnership Framework creates new opportunities to expand cooperation in economic diversification, private sector development, productivity growth and sustainable economic development. Babayev also outlined government efforts to maintain macroeconomic stability, strengthen fiscal sustainability, improve public financial management, enhance budget efficiency and gradually reduce dependence on oil and gas revenues. He stressed the importance of developing the non-oil sector, attracting private investment and expanding export potential. He further outlined public financial management reforms, including the development of the Digital Public Finance Information System, the expansion of programme- and performance-based budgeting, and the digitalization of public procurement. He emphasized the importance of continued cooperation with the World Bank in these areas. The meeting also focused on reforms in the financial management and oversight of state-owned enterprises, including efforts to improve financial discipline, corporate governance and dividend policies, as well as manage potential fiscal risks. The sides discussed opportunities to expand cooperation with the World Bank in these areas. The sides reviewed preparations for the Global Conference on State-Owned Enterprises, scheduled to take place in Baku in April 2027 in partnership with the World Bank Group. The conference is expected to provide a platform for sharing international experience in strengthening the governance and financial sustainability of state-owned enterprises. The parties also discussed a draft Report on the Observance of Standards and Codes (ROSC) in accounting and auditing, prepared with World Bank support, and its recommendations. They stressed the importance of improving relevant legislation, enhancing the quality and transparency of financial reporting, strengthening audit oversight and continuing dialogue on outstanding issues. Discussions also covered the next phase of the World Bank’s analytical work on economic growth and diversification, as well as potential investment projects in agriculture, water resource management, transport and urban infrastructure. World Bank representatives welcomed the development of the partnership with Azerbaijan and expressed their readiness to continue technical, analytical and financial cooperation in support of the country’s economic and institutional reforms, public financial management and state-owned enterprise sector.

Yupay Thu, 11/12/2026 - 11:39 Christopher Gangemi By November 12, 2026 After a handful of “small cell” wireless poles that sprang up in Northwest Woods and Wainscott proved controversial, and with more than 150 more planned within a year, the East Hampton Town Board decided on Tuesday to change course. While the problematic poles — which contain equipment to improve wireless coverage and service — are metal and of the “stealth” variety, the board seemed eager to move instead toward wooden poles, with the telecommunications equipment hung on the outside in plain sight. “They’re not really small if you’re putting them in an area without any existing infrastructure,” admitted Elizabeth Herington-Smith, general manager of Cityscape Consultants, which advises the town on wireless decisions. “They’re small in comparison to large macro towers, but they’re not really small.” The board decided to post a survey for town residents on its website, which Tina Vavilis LaGarenne, director of the Planning Department, said she would develop quickly with Cityscape. To implement the survey, the board would have to amend the contract under which Cityscape currently operates. “Now, the community has had an opportunity to see them 3-D on the street,” said Councilwoman Cate Rogers. “I think it would be a good time to bring them in again and say, ‘Now that they’re here, what do you think?’ “ Until survey data is compiled and analyzed, wooden poles will be used on open applications. “I do hear a majority of the board preferring wood, loud and clear,” said Ms. Vavilis LaGarenne. She noted that there had been a “visceral” reaction to the metal poles. “The cement base looks out of character for the community,” said Town Supervisor Kathee Burke-Gonzalez, a remark that led to a discussion of whether the concrete could be tinted. (Answer: It could.) All told, the discussion lasted over an hour. The planning director showed the board pictures of poles already installed and the board offered critiques and discussed preferences. When the town originally developed its wireless code, it used a survey to gauge the public’s design preference. Sixty-one percent of respondents (out of more than 500 people who participated) indicated that they liked the “stealth” poles. Most comments, though, reflected a desire for improved service, and a fear that public safety could be impacted by inconsistent wireless coverage. Only Councilman Tom Flight, who announced at the meeting that he would serve just one more year on the board, showed a strong preference for the metal poles, which he called “critical infrastructure.” Metal, he said, is “more resilient.” If the poles are better screened, he suggested, complaints based on aesthetics could decrease. “What’s the wind speed resilience of the wooden poles?” Mr. Flight asked. “I can certainly get that information,” said Ms. Herington-Smith. Councilman Ian Calder-Piedmonte said he did not have a strong opinion on the pole material, either way. Whether the poles were wooden or metal, he said, people may not appreciate a pole suddenly appearing at the edge of their lawn. For him, it was more about placement, screening, and matching a neighborhood’s existing conditions. “The one in Wainscott, it’s hard to imagine that in a worse location,” he said, referring to a pole erected where Wainscott Stone Road meets Sayre’s Path. To address the placement concern, Ms. Vavilis LaGarenne presented the board with draft code that would require small cell poles to be placed among massed trees. “Our code currently doesn’t require that,” she said, noting that the setting was stark for both the pole at the Wainscott intersection and another on Montauk Avenue in Northwest Woods that also had proved unpopular with neighboring residents. The board seemed supportive, even though she warned them that placing the poles near trees might necessitate “heavy pruning” or perhaps even the loss of some trees. For poles that could not be placed near tree masses, another section of draft code that the board seemed to like would require screening vegetation to be planted at the base of the poles. Ms. Herington-Smith said the shrubbery could allowed to grow tall, since “the antenna is where the signal is propagated.” Screening that covered the lower half of the pole should not affect service, she said. “Could the screening be native?” asked Ms. Burke-Gonzalez. “Yes,” said Ms. Vavilis LaGarenne. “It’s important that stuff like this is in our code, because if it’s not published in advance, it’s hard for us.” (The Federal Communications Commission has made it difficult for municipalities to regulate cellphone towers.) “We are held to what’s in our code,” Ms. Vavilis LaGarenne emphasized. “Do we just want to say that the screening should be native?”

articles.content: War in Ukraine: Putin Meets with envoys from the U.S. President | Africanews War in Ukraine: Putin Meets with envoys from the U.S. President Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday at the Kremlin with envoys from U.S. President Donald Trump for talks on the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Washington sought to give new momentum to peace efforts following two days of negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, held under U.S. auspices in the United Arab Emirates. These were the first direct talks between Russian and Ukrainian officials in nine months, as peace efforts had stalled this year. Although they had just concluded two days of negotiations between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates—which ended Wednesday with an agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange— but failed to yield any visible progress toward ending nearly five years of large-scale hostilities, U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff appeared determined to seize the opportunity and traveled directly to the Kremlin. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders on Thursday against discussions between the United States and Russia regarding a new security agreement for the continent. articles.content: Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch are getting gesture control for Android XR Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air will be able to control Android XR glasses with gestures Android XR glasses get their own control wearable, but you might already own it. Google says the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch will be able to control Android XR glasses. just launched its line of Intelligent Eyewear glasses. The smart glasses run on Android XR with hardware built by Samsung. They start at $395, with pre-orders opening up today through both Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. For all the smart features they have, one of the best might be the sly integration Google is setting up between Intelligent Eyewear and its existing wearables. Google quietly noted that both Pixel Watch models and the Fitbit Air will be able to control Android XR glasses, like a dedicated control band some competitor smart glasses come with. Pixel Watch already supports gesture controls using sensors to detect movements like finger pinching or wrist adjustments. Google’s Android XR demo included pausing and playing music using a pinch gesture. We imagine gesture controls will support as much as the touchpad that sits in the arms of Intelligent Eyewear models, though it’s not clear what gestures will be supported just yet. You’ll still be able to use the touch sensors, but Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air will be just another avenue. According to what Google told us, the Pixel Watch will be supported around launch, with Fitbit Air adding support sometime in 2027. Galaxy Watch will also be supported on Samsung devices. articles.title: OpenAI Commits $2 Million to AI Safety Research for Children
articles.desc: OpenAI pledges $2M to study AI's impact on children, signing the Charter of Engagement for Safer AI at the Paris Peace Forum. (Read More)
articles.content: OpenAI Commits $2 Million to AI Safety Research for Children - Blockchain.News OpenAI has announced a $2 million commitment to support research on artificial intelligence (AI) and its impact on children’s safety and wellbeing. The pledge was made during the Paris Peace Forum, where OpenAI signed the Charter of Engagement for Safer AI for Children. This initiative is part of a broader effort to establish global standards for youth AI safety and foster collaboration among governments, researchers, civil society, and industry stakeholders. Focus on Measuring Risks and Opportunities The funding will support the scientific research network under the Coalition for Children’s Rights and Protection in the Age of AI. OpenAI’s contribution aims to develop shared tools that researchers can use to measure AI’s risks and opportunities for young people. These tools are intended to inform the creation of safer AI products and more effective policy frameworks. The Charter of Engagement outlines principles for safe, age-appropriate AI, alongside a research program that ensures the independence of findings. Research teams will retain control over their conclusions, with all results—positive, negative, or inconclusive—published to promote transparency and accountability. This initiative builds on OpenAI’s previous advocacy for comprehensive youth AI safety legislation. The organization has called for frameworks that include age-appropriate safeguards, tools for parents, regular risk assessments, and meaningful accountability measures. OpenAI emphasized its commitment to collaborating with European policymakers on the EU Kids Act and engaging with global partners to enhance protections and opportunities for young people. By supporting this research, OpenAI aims to address the dual challenge of maximizing AI’s benefits for children while mitigating risks to their safety and development. The findings are expected to contribute to the development of practical safeguards and evidence-based policies that prioritize children’s rights and wellbeing in the age of AI. articles.desc: Zero-size graphics can derail printing, while some admins also face activation failures
articles.content: Microsoft has an image problem with November's Windows security update Microsoft has an image problem with November's Windows security update Zero-size graphics can derail printing, while some admins also face activation failures Singapore says US authorities, and Supermicro, hardly helped investigation of Jensen Huang’s Chinese friend Alibaba's Qwen3.8 re-educated with a more Western worldview DOJ takes aim at $1.2B in Binance loot as FBI disrupts North Korean scam Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune Google promises its new smart specs won't give creeps their ideal view Printing with Windows has always been something of a choose-your-own-adventure, and November's security update has added another unwelcome plot twist: documents containing certain images might not print. The issue affects images rendered with a height or width of zero at the selected printing resolution. These might not be visible to users, but can form part of a document's watermarking or layout. After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too. Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected." According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016. Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected. Users need not have added these objects themselves. Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible. Printer problems aren't the only issue requiring attention. After installation of the November 2026 security update, Microsoft warned that "certain Windows activation and licensing operations performed using the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) might fail." This one is a little more niche, but it could be a headache for affected administrators. It primarily affects organizations that use command-line tools or automated processes to manage Windows activation and licensing. ), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said. "The failure has been observed while executing the command ' The notice (WI1549486) currently lists Windows 11 23H2, Windows 10 22H2 and 21H2, and Windows Server 2025, 2022, and 2019 as affected. The printing problem remains under investigation, but Microsoft says a fix for the activation issue is due in the coming days.
